text:
ben: follow-up from the CP separation RFC — idea: run a federated set of short-lived "anchor clusters" per region that advertise affinity tokens to clients. want to capture tradeoffs for private installs and streaming.
yara: +1 to affinity tokens. they let us route streams to the same anchor without sticky IPs. main question: how do we sign/verify tokens for air-gapped customers?
om: for hosted, global signer issues tokens. for Private, allow an offline signing bundle or a customer-owned signer (public key uploaded). require bundle rotation window and serials.
lucy: offline bundles are fine but revocation is painful. propose bundle includes a short TTL (hours) and a revocation serial list that customers can fetch via local agent. docs must highlight clock skew risks.
ben: agreed. propose default token TTL 300s for streams, 30s for control RPCs. tokens carry anchor_id, az_hint, issued_at, expiry, and a hmac/sig. clients present token on reconnect to resume KV window.\yyara: discovery: prefer local agent socket (if present) -> SRV -> registry API. low TTL SRV is ok for hosted, but Private should have explicit local discovery first. timeouts: local 25ms, SRV 150ms, registry 400ms.
om: streaming semantics: clients should support resume with token + last-seq. anchor returns delta if possible. if delta unavailable, anchor signals cold-bootstrap. we need metrics for resume_success and cold_boot_fraction.
lucy: cache prewarm: two modes — full replicate hot-set (bandwidth heavy) or prioritized prefetch (stream hot prefixes). make prefetch API opt-in for Private. example: POST /v1/anchor/prefetch {"priority": "hot", "limit": 200}. returns 202 + progress events.\yara: handoff consistency: want a graceful handoff that avoids split-brain. ops flow: 1) new anchor obtains leaf cert, 2) old anchor enters DRAIN, emits DRAIN_WINDOW=N seconds, writes mirrored if writes enabled, 3) new anchor becomes authoritative after window. provide forced-cutover option with documented risk.
ben: mirror writes are hard for strongly consistent ops. prefer a short write-block window for critical state (e.g., prefix writes) and mirror for non-critical telemetry. ops must be able to set per-customer policy.
om: what about connectivity modes? direct-quic to anchors vs in-VPC proxy. proxy gives stable egress IPs (good for whitelisting) but adds cost. default to direct, proxy opt-in per-customer or per-route.
lucy: QUIC helps resume across migrations because of connectionless resume tickets — good for streaming. but for Private, middlebox compatibility might force TCP+TLS option. SDK should expose enable_quic flag and a connect_mode enum.
yara: metrics/tracing: tag with anchor_id, token_serial, bundle_serial (if present). emit cp.handoff.duration, anchor.prefetch_bytes, stream.resume_latency, token_validation_failures.
ben: ops surface: Console should show current anchors (active/draining/standby), last_bundle_serial, scheduled rotations, and manual drain/cutover buttons. deploy-bot: rotation enqueued for region-eu-1 at 2026-04-02T03:00Z (id=rot-7c2).
lucy: security note: for customer-signed bundles, require explicit acceptance in Console and an audit trail. prefer global-signer for hosted. record who uploaded bundle and bundle serial in traces.
om: action items: 1) yara + lucy write offline-bundle lifecycle + revocation playbook, 2) ben + om draft SDK discovery + token defaults + resume contract, 3) infra to prototype prefetch API and gather bandwidth numbers for top-200 vs top-500 prefixes.
yara: I'll start bundle doc and include clock-skew mitigation tips.
ben: I'll draft SDK PR with configs: discovery_order, timeouts_ms, connect_mode, enable_quic, token_ttl_s, and sample code.
lucy: infra-bot: perf spike scheduled — SRV vs local-agent discovery + QUIC vs TCP on Thu 05:00 UTC.
ben: thanks all — keeping thread open for RFC follow-up and will sync into the main RFC doc.
